chapter.li: LEChapter16 Verse1 In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple. VerseEnd Verse2 Above it stood the seraphims. Each one had six wings: with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly. VerseEnd Verse3 And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts! The whole earth is full of his glory! VerseEnd Verse4 And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke. VerseEnd

Verse5 Then said I, Woe is unto me, for I am undone because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts. VerseEnd Verse6 Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar. VerseEnd Verse7 And he laid upon my mouth and said, Lo, this hath touched 2PSI thy lips, and 2PSI thine iniquity is taken away, and 2PSI thy sin purged. VerseEnd Verse8 Also, I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send? And who will go for us? Then I said, Here am I; send me. VerseEnd Verse9 And he said, Go and tell this people, Hear 2PP ye indeed — but they understand not; and, See 2PP ye indeed — but they perceived not. VerseEnd Verse10 Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and be healed. VerseEnd Verse11 Then said I, Lord, how long? And he said, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate, VerseEnd Verse12 and the Lord have removed men far away; for there shall be a great forsaking in the midst of the land. VerseEnd Verse13 But yet in it there shall be a tenth, and they shall return and shall be eaten as a teil tree and as an oak, whose substance is in them when they cast their leaves, so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof. VerseEnd

LEChapter17 Verse1 And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah king of Judah, that Rezin king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel, went up towards Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it. VerseEnd Verse2 And it was told the house of David, saying, Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind. VerseEnd

Verse3 Then said the Lord unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz — 2PSI thou, and Shear-jashub 2PSI thy son — at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field. VerseEnd Verse4 And say unto him, Take heed and be quiet; fear not, neither be faint-hearted for the two tails of these smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah, VerseEnd Verse5 because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah have taken evil counsel against 2PSI thee, saying, VerseEnd Verse6 Let us go up against Judah and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set a king in the midst of it, yea, the son of Tabeal. VerseEnd Verse7 Thus saith the Lord God: It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass. VerseEnd Verse8 For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus, Rezin. And within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people. VerseEnd Verse9 And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If 2PP ye will not believe, surely 2PP ye shall not be established. VerseEnd

Verse10 Moreover, the Lord spake again unto Ahaz, saying, VerseEnd Verse11 Ask 2PSI thee a sign of the Lord 2PSI thy God; ask either in the depths or in the heights above. VerseEnd Verse12 But Ahaz said, I will not ask, neither will I tempt the Lord. VerseEnd Verse13 And he said, Hear 2PP ye now, O house of David: Is it a small thing for 2PP you to weary men, but will 2PP ye weary my God also? VerseEnd Verse14 Therefore, the Lord himself shall give 2PP you a sign: behold, a virgin shall conceive, and shall bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. VerseEnd Verse15 Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil and to choose the good. VerseEnd Verse16 For before the child shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land that 2PSI thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings. VerseEnd Verse17 The Lord shall bring upon 2PSI thee, and upon 2PSI thy people, and upon 2PSI thy father’s house — days that have not come from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah — the king of Assyria. VerseEnd Verse18 And it shall come to pass in that day that the Lord shall hiss for the fly that is in the uttermost part of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria. VerseEnd Verse19 And they shall come and shall rest all of them in the desolate valleys, and in the holes of the rocks, and upon all thorns, and upon all bushes. VerseEnd Verse20 In the same day shall the Lord shave with a razor that is hired — by them beyond the river, by the king of Assyria — the head, and the hair of the feet; and it shall also consume the beard. VerseEnd

Verse21 And it shall come to pass that in that day, a man shall nourish a young cow and two sheep. VerseEnd Verse22 And it shall come to pass, for the abundance of milk they shall give, he shall eat butter; for butter and honey shall everyone eat that is left in the land. VerseEnd Verse23 And it shall come to pass in that day, every place shall be, where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings, which shall be for briers and thorns. VerseEnd Verse24 With arrows and with bows shall men come thither because all the land shall become briers and thorns. VerseEnd Verse25 And all hills that shall be digged with the mattock, there shall not come thither the fear of briers and thorns, but it shall be for the sending forth of oxen, and the treading of lesser cattle. VerseEnd

LEChapter18 Verse1 Moreover, the word of the Lord said unto me, Take 2PSI thee a great roll and write in it with a man’s pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz. VerseEnd Verse2 And I took unto me faithful witnesses to record — Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah. VerseEnd Verse3 And I went unto the prophetess, and she conceived and bare a son. Then said the Lord to me, Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz. VerseEnd Verse4 For behold, the child shall not have knowledge to cry, My father and my mother — before the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria. VerseEnd

Verse5 The Lord spake also unto me again, saying, VerseEnd Verse6 Forasmuch as this people refuseth the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son, VerseEnd Verse7 now therefore behold, the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria and all his glory. And he shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks, VerseEnd Verse8 and he shall pass through Judah. He shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck. And the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of 2PSI thy land, O Immanuel. VerseEnd Verse9 Associate yourselves, O 2PP ye people, and 2PP ye shall be broken in pieces. And give ear, all 2PP ye of far countries: Gird yourselves, and 2PP ye shall be broken in pieces; gird yourselves, and 2PP ye shall be broken in pieces. VerseEnd Verse10 Take counsel together, and it shall come to naught; speak the word, and it shall not stand; for God is with us. VerseEnd

Verse11 For the Lord spake thus to me with a strong hand, and instructed me that I should not walk in the way of this people, saying, VerseEnd Verse12 Say 2PP ye not, A confederacy — to all to whom this people shall say, A confederacy; neither fear 2PP ye their fear nor be afraid. VerseEnd Verse13 Sanctify the Lord of Hosts himself, and let him be 2PP your fear, and let him be 2PP your dread, VerseEnd Verse14 and he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offense to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse15 And many among them shall stumble and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken. VerseEnd

Verse16 Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples. VerseEnd Verse17 And I will wait upon the Lord that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him. VerseEnd Verse18 Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of Hosts which dwelleth in Mount Zion. VerseEnd Verse19 And when they shall say unto 2PP you, Seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and unto wizards that peep and mutter — should not a people seek unto their God? For the living to hear from the dead — VerseEnd Verse20 to the law and to the testimony? And if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them. VerseEnd Verse21 And they shall pass through it hardly bestead and hungry; and it shall come to pass that when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse their king and their God, and look upward. VerseEnd Verse22 And they shall look unto the earth and behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish, and shall be driven to darkness. VerseEnd

LEChapter19 Verse1 Nevertheless, the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun, and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict by the way of the Red Sea beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations. VerseEnd Verse2 The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light; they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined. VerseEnd Verse3 2PSI Thou hast multiplied the nation and increased the joy; they joy before 2PSI thee according to the joy in harvest, and as men rejoice when they divide the spoil. VerseEnd Verse4 For 2PSI thou hast broken the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, VerseEnd Verse5 for every battle of the warrior with confused noise and garments rolled in blood; but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire. VerseEnd Verse6 For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, and the government shall be upon his shoulder. And his name shall be called Wonderful Counselor, the Mighty God, the Everlasting Father, the Prince of Peace. VerseEnd Verse7 Of the increase of government and peace there is no end, upon the throne of David and upon his kingdom, to order it and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of Hosts will perform this. VerseEnd

Verse8 The Lord sent his word unto Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. VerseEnd Verse9 And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, that say in the pride and the stoutness of heart, VerseEnd Verse10 The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones; the sycamores are cut down, but we will change them into cedars. VerseEnd Verse11 Therefore, the Lord shall set up the adversaries of Rezin against him and join his enemies together — VerseEnd Verse12 the Syrians before and the Philistines behind — and they shall devour Israel with open mouth. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand stretched out still. VerseEnd

Verse13 For the people turneth not unto him that smiteth them, neither do they seek the Lord of Hosts. VerseEnd Verse14 Therefore will the Lord cut off from Israel head and tail, branch and rush, in one day. VerseEnd Verse15 The ancient, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail. VerseEnd Verse16 For the leaders of this people cause them to err, and they that are led of them are destroyed. VerseEnd Verse17 Therefore, the Lord shall have no joy in their young men, neither shall have mercy on their fatherless and widows; for every one of them is a hypocrite and an evildoer, and every mouth speaketh folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand stretched out still. VerseEnd

Verse18 For wickedness burneth as the fire; it shall devour the briers and thorns, and shall kindle in the thickets of the forests, and they shall mount up like the lifting up of smoke. VerseEnd Verse19 Through the wrath of the Lord of Hosts is the land darkened, and the people shall be as the fuel of the fire; no man shall spare his brother. VerseEnd Verse20 And he shall snatch on the right hand and be hungry, and he shall eat on the left hand and they shall not be satisfied. They shall eat, every man, the flesh of his own arm: VerseEnd Verse21 Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh; they together shall be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand stretched out still. VerseEnd

LEChapter20 Verse1 Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees and that write grievousness which they have prescribed, VerseEnd Verse2 to turn aside the needy from judgment and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey and that they may rob the fatherless. VerseEnd Verse3 And what will 2PP ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? To whom will 2PP ye flee for help? And where will 2PP ye leave 2PP your glory? VerseEnd Verse4 Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand stretched out still. VerseEnd

Verse5 O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is their indignation. VerseEnd Verse6 I will send him against a hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets. VerseEnd Verse7 Howbeit he meaneth not so, neither doth his heart think so, but in his heart it is to destroy and cut off nations not a few. VerseEnd Verse8 For he saith, Are not my princes altogether kings? VerseEnd Verse9 Is not Calno as Carchemish? Is not Hamath as Arpad? Is not Samaria as Damascus? VerseEnd Verse10 As my hand hath founded the kingdoms of the idols, and whose graven images did excel them of Jerusalem and of Samaria, VerseEnd Verse11 shall I not, as I have done unto Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and to her idols? VerseEnd

Verse12 Wherefore, it shall come to pass that when the Lord hath performed his whole work upon Mount Zion and upon Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of his high looks. VerseEnd Verse13 For he saith, By the strength of my hand and by my wisdom I have done these things, for I am prudent. And I have removed the borders of the people, and have robbed their treasures, and I have put down the inhabitants like a valiant man. VerseEnd Verse14 And my hand hath found as a nest the riches of the people, and as one gathereth eggs that are left have I gathered all the earth; and there was none that moved the wing, or opened the mouth, or peeped. VerseEnd Verse15 Shall the ax boast itself against him that heweth therewith? Shall the saw magnify itself against him that shaketh it? As if the rod should shake itself against them that lift it up, or as if the staff should lift up itself as if it were no wood. VerseEnd Verse16 Therefore shall the Lord, the Lord of Hosts, send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory he shall kindle a burning like the burning of a fire. VerseEnd Verse17 And the Light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame, and shall burn and shall devour his thorns and his briers in one day, VerseEnd Verse18 and shall consume the glory of his forest and of his fruitful field, both soul and body. And they shall be as when a standard-bearer fainteth. VerseEnd Verse19 And the rest of the trees of his forest shall be few, that a child may write them. VerseEnd

Verse20 And it shall come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again stay upon him that smote them, but shall stay upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. VerseEnd Verse21 The remnant shall return, yea, even the remnant of Jacob, unto the mighty God. VerseEnd Verse22 For though 2PSI thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return. The consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness; VerseEnd Verse23 for the Lord God of Hosts shall make a consumption, even determined, in all the land. VerseEnd

Verse24 Therefore, thus saith the Lord God of Hosts: O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of the Assyrian (he shall smite 2PSI thee with a rod, and shall lift up his staff against 2PSI thee, after the manner of Egypt), VerseEnd Verse25 for yet a very little while, and the indignation shall cease and mine anger in their destruction. VerseEnd Verse26 And the Lord of Hosts shall stir up a scourge for him, according to the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb; and as his rod was upon the sea, so shall he lift it up after the manner of Egypt. VerseEnd Verse27 And it shall come to pass in that day, that his burden shall be taken away from off 2PSI thy shoulder, and his yoke from off 2PSI thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing. VerseEnd

Verse28 He is come to Aiath, he is passed to Migron; at Michmash, he hath laid up his carriages. VerseEnd Verse29 They are gone over the passage, they have taken up their lodging at Geba. Ramath is afraid, Gibeah of Saul is fled. VerseEnd Verse30 Lift up the voice, O daughter of Gallim; cause it to be heard unto Laish, O poor Anathoth. VerseEnd Verse31 Madmenah is removed, the inhabitants of Gebim gather themselves to flee. VerseEnd Verse32 As yet shall he remain at Nob that day; he shall shake his hand against the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse33 Behold, the Lord, the Lord of Hosts shall lop the bough with terror, and the high ones of stature shall be hewn down, and the haughty shall be humbled. VerseEnd Verse34 And he shall cut down the thickets of the forests with iron, and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one. VerseEnd

LEChapter21 Verse1 And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots. VerseEnd Verse2 And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him — the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord — VerseEnd Verse3 and shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord. And he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears, VerseEnd Verse4 but with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth. And he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked. VerseEnd Verse5 And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins. VerseEnd Verse6 The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf, and the young lion, and the fatling together, and a little child shall lead them. VerseEnd Verse7 And the cow and the bear shall feed, their young ones shall lie down together, and the lion shall eat straw like the ox. VerseEnd Verse8 And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice’s den. VerseEnd Verse9 They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea. VerseEnd

Verse10 And in that day, there shall be a root of Jesse which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the gentiles seek, and his rest shall be glorious. VerseEnd Verse11 And it shall come to pass in that day that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people which shall be left from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. VerseEnd Verse12 And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah, from the four corners of the earth. VerseEnd Verse13 The envy of Ephraim also shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off. Ephraim shall not envy Judah and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. VerseEnd Verse14 But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west, they shall spoil them of the east together, they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon shall obey them. VerseEnd Verse15 And the Lord shall utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea, and with his mighty wind he shall shake his hand over the river, and shall smite it in the seven streams, and make men go over dry-shod. VerseEnd Verse16 And there shall be a highway for the remnant of his people which shall be left from Assyria, like as it was to Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt. VerseEnd

LEChapter22 Verse1 And in that day, 2PSI thou shalt say, O Lord, I will praise 2PSI thee; though 2PSI thou wast angry with me, 2PSI thine anger is turned away and 2PSI thou comfortedst me. VerseEnd Verse2 Behold, God is my salvation. I will trust and not be afraid, for the Lord Jehovah is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation. VerseEnd Verse3 Therefore, with joy shall 2PP ye draw water out of the wells of salvation. VerseEnd Verse4 And in that day shall 2PP ye say, Praise the Lord, call upon his name, declare his doings among the people, make mention that his name is exalted. VerseEnd Verse5 Sing unto the Lord, for he hath done excellent things; this is known in all the earth. VerseEnd Verse6 Cry out and shout, 2PSI thou inhabitant of Zion, for great is the Holy One of Israel in the midst of 2PSI thee. VerseEnd
